cards.name: Bas Relief
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery, Sketch) that turns the artwork into a low-relief carving lit from one side: dark areas take one tone and light areas the other, so in Illustrator the result is a grey stone-like surface where shape edges read as raised ridges with a highlight on one side and a shadow on the other.
use_for: carved-stone or plaque look for a logo or emblem on a poster
faux coin, medal or seal artwork
embossed monochrome background texture built from a pattern or illustration
quick sculpted-relief preview of a vector mark before modelling it properly
avoid: Colour is discarded: in Illustrator the Sketch effects draw in black and white (every harvest render of the red/blue probe came out greyscale). To keep colour, apply it to an extra fill in the Appearance panel and set that fill to Multiply or Overlay, or colour the result in Photoshop.

Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Photoshop (Filter Gallery) effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB). From Adobe's documentation, not tested by the harvest, whose probes all ran in new RGB documents.
Real raised 3D lettering with depth and colour: use Effect > 3D and Materials > Inflate or Extrude & Bevel instead.
Anything that must stay crisp and scalable (logos for print, small type): the result is a raster at the Document Raster Effects resolution, not vector.

Flat single-colour fills: the scripted harvest render (fallback settings) turned the flat red probe into a plain grey ramp, dark at the top to light at the bottom, with no carved edges (Effect_Sketch_Bas_Relief.png); it needs shapes, type or tonal detail to carve.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send this effect's settings (they sit in a binary descriptor); use a saved Graphic Style, the menu command plus its dialog, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog.

params.name: Detail
params.does: how much fine edge detail is carved into the relief; high keeps small shapes and type edges
params.typical: 13 (harvest dialog value) for crisp carving, low values for a soft blobby relief

params.name: Smoothness
params.does: smooths the carved surface; higher removes small ridges and noise
params.typical: 1-3 for sharp carving, higher for a softened cast look

params.name: Light Direction
params.does: side the light comes from; decides which edges get the highlight and which the shadow
params.typical: Top Left or Top for a natural carved read; Bottom (harvest value) looks inverted/debossed

pairs_with: Effect > Texture > Grain for a rough stone surface
an extra fill set to Multiply in the Appearance panel to tint the relief
Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings (set 300 ppi for print before judging texture size)
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_BsRl"><Dict data="I dataSize 68 I PrevDres 300 B go 1"/></LiveEffect>') applies the live effect, but Detail / Smoothness / Light Direction live in the binary 'data' descriptor that Dict data cannot carry, so a scripted apply renders with whatever settings the plug-in falls back to (harvest render check: it did change the probe, mean diff 11.008, but not with chosen values). For chosen values: select the item and app.executeMenuCommand('Live PSAdapter_plugin_BsRl'), which opens the 'Bas Relief (100%)' dialog with the last-used values and needs OK; or build the look once by hand, save it as a Graphic Style and apply it with doc.graphicStyles.getByName('<style>').applyTo(item). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel (double-click to edit); Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: rasterizes the object at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded) through the Filter Gallery; slows redraw on large artwork

review.changes: CMYK avoid line marked as documentation, not harvest-tested (all probes ran in RGB documents); avoid: added what the probe render shows (flat red fill -> plain dark-top/light-bottom grey ramp, no carving)

verified.note: The photo becomes a grey stone-like low relief lit from the top left, every edge a raised ridge with a highlight on one side and a shadow on the other (maximum chroma 0: pure greyscale, as the Sketch colour-discard avoid line says), as the card describes.

Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live effect in the Appearance panel (double-click to edit); Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into an embedded image
cards.cost: medium: rasterizes the object at the Document Raster Effects resolution (PrevDres 300 recorded) through the Filter Gallery; slows redraw on large artwork

review.changes: CMYK avoid line marked as documentation, not harvest-tested (all probes ran in RGB documents)

verified.note: The photo is simplified into embossed handmade paper with grain, the darker shapes reading as cut sheets raised or sunk against the lighter paper (maximum chroma 0: pure greyscale, as the Sketch colour-discard avoid line says), as the card describes.

cards.name: Photocopy
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery, Sketch) that simulates a photocopy: large dark areas are copied only around their edges and midtones fall away to solid black or white. The harvest probe (red rectangle, blue stroke) became a white box with a black outline, which is the typical result on flat vector art.
use_for: xerox / zine / punk-flyer look on a placed photo
high-contrast black-and-white outline treatment of an illustration
gritty photocopied texture for a gig poster
avoid: Colour is discarded: in Illustrator the Sketch effects draw in black and white (every harvest render of the red/blue probe came out greyscale). To keep colour, apply it to an extra fill in the Appearance panel and set that fill to Multiply or Overlay, or colour the result in Photoshop.

Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Photoshop (Filter Gallery) effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB). From Adobe's documentation, not tested by the harvest, whose probes all ran in new RGB documents.
Solid colour areas you want to keep solid: they hollow out to outlines; use Threshold-like art (Image Trace in Black and White mode) instead.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send this effect's settings (they sit in a binary descriptor); use a saved Graphic Style, the menu command plus its dialog, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog.

params.name: Detail
params.does: how much detail survives around edges

params.name: Darkness
params.does: how dark and heavy the copied edges and shadows are

pairs_with: Effect > Texture > Grain for copier noise
an extra fill set to Multiply to put a colour behind the copy
Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings (set 300 ppi for print before judging texture size)

cards.name: Plaster
cards.summary: Photoshop Effect (Filter Gallery, Sketch) that moulds the artwork out of 3D plaster: dark areas are raised and light areas sunken, lit from one side, giving a glossy, blobby relief; in Illustrator it is greyscale (the harvest's flat red probe went solid black: on flat fills it only remaps brightness, Illustrator's own result).
use_for: molten or moulded-plaster abstract texture
liquid / clay relief treatment of bold shapes for a poster background
sculpted-surface look on a placed photo
avoid: Colour is discarded: in Illustrator the Sketch effects draw in black and white (every harvest render of the red/blue probe came out greyscale). To keep colour, apply it to an extra fill in the Appearance panel and set that fill to Multiply or Overlay, or colour the result in Photoshop.

Greyed out in CMYK documents: the Photoshop (Filter Gallery) effects need an RGB document (File > Document Color Mode > RGB). From Adobe's documentation, not tested by the harvest, whose probes all ran in new RGB documents.
Logos and type: edges melt into blobs; for a clean raised look use Effect > 3D and Materials > Inflate.
Image Balance at an extreme: the whole object floods to black or white.

Scripted pipelines that need chosen values: applyEffect cannot send this effect's settings (they sit in a binary descriptor); use a saved Graphic Style, the menu command plus its dialog, or the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog.

params.name: Image Balance
params.does: tonal split that decides which areas are raised versus sunken

params.name: Smoothness
params.does: how rounded and melted the relief is; high values are smoother blobs

params.name: Light Direction
params.does: side the light comes from on the relief

pairs_with: an extra fill set to Overlay or Multiply to tint the plaster
a gradient underneath so there are tones to mould
Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings (set 300 ppi for print before judging texture size)
